Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

on preposition

on a surface

also upon, onto

classical

Hor. C. 2.16.13–14: splendet in mēnsā tenuī salīnum
Petr. 29.1: in pariete erat pictus

in (+ ablative)

preposition with the ablative

on (resting on)

Latin does not tell “on” from “in”: in mēnsā, on the table; in pariete, on the wall; in terrā, on earth. For “on top of”, super (see on top of).

Other words

  • in (+ accusative) — onto, on (where to)

    preposition with the accusative · classical · Cic. Sen. 34: in equum omnīnō nōn ascendere

    Of motion onto a thing: in equum ascendere, get on a horse; in mēnsam, onto the table.

  • equō, umerō (ablative alone) — on (horseback, one’s shoulder)

    ablative without a preposition · also used · classical · Mor. 81: vēnālēs umerō fascēs portābat in urbem; Cic. Sen. 34: cum autem equō

    With verbs of carrying and riding the ablative often stands alone: equō vehī, ride on a horse; umerō portāre, carry on one’s shoulder.

Examples

  • vīvitur parvō bene, cui paternum splendet in mēnsā tenuī salīnum

    he lives well on little whose father’s salt-cellar shines on a plain tableHor. C. 2.16.13–14

  • canis ingēns, catēnā vīnctus, in pariete erat pictus

    a huge dog on a chain was painted on the wallPetr. 29.1

  • Glōria in altissimīs Deō, et in terrā pāx hominibus bonae voluntātis.

    Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.Vulg. Lc. 2.14

  • cum ingressus iter pedibus sit, in equum omnīnō nōn ascendere; cum autem equō, ex equō nōn dēscendere

    when he has set out on foot, he will not get on a horse at all; but when on horseback, he will not get offCic. Sen. 34

  • vēnālēs umerō fascēs portābat in urbem

    he used to carry bundles for sale on his shoulder into townMor. 81

See also on top of, in, off, above.
